3.  **Brainstorming/Outline:**

   - *Body 2:* Community & open-source philosophy (collaboration, transparency, security)

4.  **Drafting (Mental Refinement & Word Count Management):**
   I'll write carefully, monitoring length. I'll aim for ~500 words total.

   *(Introduction)* Linux stands as one of the most transformative pieces of software in modern computing history. Born in 1991 as a personal project by Finnish computer science student Linus Torvalds, Linux began as a modest attempt to create a free, Unix-like operating system. What started as a hobby quickly evolved into a global movement, driven by the open-source philosophy that software should be freely shared, modified, and improved by anyone. Today, Linux powers everything from smartphones and supercomputers to web servers and cloud infrastructure, cementing its status as the backbone of the digital age.

   *(Body 1 - Architecture & Flexibility)* At its core, Linux is a kernel—the fundamental component that manages hardware resources and enables communication between software and physical devices. Unlike proprietary operating systems, Linux is distributed through numerous “distros,” each tailored to specific needs. Whether for developers, artists, or enterprise environments, users can choose from hundreds of distributions like Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, or Arch Linux.
